extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent applicants/owners, USPTO officials, litigants and judges handling U.S. patent matters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts statutory standards and procedural requirements from the America Invents Act (Public Law 112–29) affecting fee rules, supplemental examination, prioritized examination, marking/false marking, best-mode, covered business-method post-grant review, jurisdictional/removal/joinder rules, and related technical amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reductions for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (3), fees charged under subsections (a), (b), and (d)(1) shall be reduced by 50 percent with respect to their application to any small business concern as defined under section 3 of the Small Business Act, and to any independent inventor or nonprofit organization as defined in regulations issued by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: any surcharge or fee charged under subsection (c) or (d) for entities covered by this paragraph shall not be higher than that required of any other entity under the same or substantially similar circumstances. Separate provision reduces the basic filing fee by 75% for entities that qualify for small-entity status if the application is filed electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for electronic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee charged under subsection (a)(1)(A) shall be reduced by 75 percent with respect to its application to any entity to which paragraph (1) applies, if the application is filed by electronic means as prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies in combination with small-entity reductions; Director may prescribe electronic filing requirements by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharges parity for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to its application to any small-entity-describe entity, any surcharge or fee charged under subsection (c) or (d) shall not be higher than the surcharge or fee required of any other entity under the same or substantially similar circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parity in surcharges and other fees between small entities and other applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination fee and program limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee of $4,800 shall be established for filing a request ... for prioritized examination of a nonprovisional application for an original utility or plant patent. In addition to the prioritized examination fee, the filing, search, and examination fees (including excess claims and application size fees), processing fee, and publication fee remain due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may prescribe conditions for acceptance and limit the number of accepted prioritized examination filings. Until regulations are prescribed: (i) no application requesting prioritized examination may contain or be amended to contain more than 4 independent claims or more than 30 total claims; (ii) Director may not accept more than 10,000 requests per fiscal year for prioritization until regulations set another limit. Small entities receive 50% reduction for prioritized examination fee. All prioritized examination fees are credited to the USPTO Appropriation Account and may be used only for specified purposes. Fee terminates when Director first sets/adjusts that fee under statutory fee-setting authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge on fees for Appropriation transition
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a surcharge of 15 percent, rounded by standard arithmetic rules, on all fees charged or authorized by subsections (a), (b), and (d)(1) of section 41, and section 132(b), of title 35, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts collected are credited to the USPTO Appropriation Account, remain available until expended, and may be used only for purposes in section 42(c)(3)(A). The surcharge takes effect 10 days after enactment and terminates with respect to a fee on the effective date of the first fee-setting/adjustment under the Director's authority for that fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination: request and Director's certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may request supplemental examination of a patent to consider, reconsider, or correct information believed to be relevant to the patent. Within 3 months after the date a request meeting requirements is received, the Director shall conduct the supplemental examination and conclude by issuing a certificate indicating whether the information presented raises a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must comply with requirements the Director may establish. The 3‑month deadline is statutory for issuing the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination following supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certificate indicates that a substantial new question of patentability is raised by one or more items of information in the request, the Director shall order reexamination of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination is conducted according to procedures established by chapter 30, except the patent owner shall not have the right to file a statement pursuant to section 304. During reexamination the Director shall address each substantial new question identified, notwithstanding chapter 30 limitations relating to patents and printed publication or other provisions of that chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of supplemental examination on enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not be held unenforceable on the basis of conduct relating to information that had not been considered, was inadequately considered, or was incorrect in a prior examination of the patent if the information was considered, reconsidered, or corrected during a supplemental examination of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The making of a request (or absence thereof) shall not be relevant to enforceability under section 282. Exceptions: does not apply to allegations pled with particularity in a civil action or certain FDA-related notices received before the supplemental exam request date; and does not apply to defenses based on information considered/reconsidered/corrected in supplemental examination if the supplemental exam and any ordered reexamination are not concluded before the date the enforcement action is brought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and regulations for supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall, by regulation, establish fees for the submission of a request for supplemental examination of a patent, and to consider each item of information submitted in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is ordered, fees applicable to ex parte reexamination proceedings under chapter 30 shall be paid in addition to supplemental examination fees. The Director shall issue regs governing form, content, and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud discovered in supplemental examination or reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director becomes aware during supplemental examination or ordered reexamination that a material fraud on the Office may have been committed in connection with the patent, the Director shall refer the matter to the Attorney General for such further action as the Attorney General may deem appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such referral shall be treated as confidential, not included in the patent file, and not disclosed to the public unless the United States charges a person with a criminal offense in connection with the referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of construction for supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section shall be construed to: (1) preclude imposition of sanctions based on criminal or antitrust laws; (2) limit authority of the Director to investigate possible misconduct and impose sanctions for misconduct in matters before the Office; or (3) limit authority of the Director to issue regs under chapter 3 relating to sanctions for misconduct by representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination protections are not a shield against criminal/antitrust sanctions or Director's misconduct investigations/regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding agreement allocation change
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 202(c)(7)(E)(i) of title 35 is amended by striking '75 percent' and inserting '15 percent', and striking '25 percent' and inserting '85 percent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifies statutory allocation percentages under the funding-agreement provisions (conforming/effect applicability to patents issued before/on/after enactment as provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax strategies deemed within the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of evaluating an invention under section 102 or 103, any strategy for reducing, avoiding, or deferring tax liability, whether known or unknown at the time of the invention or application, shall be deemed insufficient to differentiate a claimed invention from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'tax liability' broadly to include Federal, State, local, and foreign laws. Exclusions: does not apply to inventions used solely for preparing a tax return/filing (including data recording/transmission/organization for such filing) or to methods/apparatus/technology/software used solely for financial management to the extent severable from any tax strategy or not limiting use of any tax strategy. Rule of construction: nothing implies other business methods are patentable or that business-method patents are valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement not a basis for invalidity/enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to disclose the best mode shall not be a basis on which any claim of a patent may be canceled or held invalid or otherwise unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends section 282 to preserve other section 112 requirements (except best mode), amends cross-references in sections 119(e)(1) and 120 to refer to section 112(a) other than best mode. Effective for proceedings commenced on or after enactment date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual marking allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends section 287(a) to permit marking by fixing on the article the word 'patent' or 'pat.' together with an address of a posting on the Internet, accessible to the public without charge, that associates the patented article with the number of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to cases pending on or commenced on or after enactment. Director must report to Congress within 3 years analyzing effectiveness, public access, legal issues, and deficiencies of virtual marking as an alternative to physical marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking: United States sole plaintiff for penalty; private damages for competitive injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 292(a) amended so only the United States may sue for the penalty authorized by the subsection. A person who has suffered a competitive injury as a result of a violation may file a civil action for recovery of damages adequate to compensate for the injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also clarifies that marking a product with matter relating to a patent that covered the product but has expired is not a violation. Amendments apply to all cases pending on or commenced on or after enactment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice of counsel evidence limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure of an infringer to obtain the advice of counsel with respect to any allegedly infringed patent, or the failure to present such advice to the court or jury, may not be used to prove that the accused infringer willfully infringed the patent or intended to induce infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies limitation on using absence of counsel/advice to infer willfulness or intent to induce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional post-grant review for covered business method patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall issue regulations establishing a transitional post-grant review proceeding for review of the validity of covered business method patents, regarded as and employing the standards/procedures of a post-grant review under chapter 32, subject to specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain statutory subsections do not apply to the transitional proceeding. Regulations must be issued within 1 year after enactment and take effect after a 1-year period. The transitional program is subject to an 8-year sunset (with petitions filed before repeal still processed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner eligibility for transitional proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not file a petition for a transitional proceeding with respect to a covered business method patent unless the person or the person's real party in interest or privy has been sued for infringement of the patent or has been charged with infringement under that patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits standing to accused infringers/parties already in litigation/charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted prior-art grounds in transitional proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner who challenges validity under section 102 or 103 (as in effect the day before the effective date set forth in section 3(n)(1)) may support such ground only on the basis of: (i) prior art described by section 102(a) (as in effect the day before the effective date); or (ii) prior art that discloses the invention more than 1 year before the US application date and would have been described by section 102(a) (as in effect the day before the effective date) if disclosed by another before the applicant's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the types of prior art grounds available to petitioners challenging covered business method patents during the transitional program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from transitional proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner in a transitional proceeding that results in a final written decision under section 328(a) with respect to a claim, or the petitioner's real party in interest, may not assert in civil actions (28 U.S.C. §1338) or ITC proceedings (section 337) that the claim is invalid on any ground that the petitioner raised during that transitional proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes estoppel: grounds raised during transitional proceeding cannot later be asserted in specified fora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of covered business method patent
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Covered business method patent' means a patent that claims a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service, except that the term does not include patents for technological inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director shall issue regulations to assist in determining whether a patent is for a technological invention; rule of construction: nothing in this section amends/interprets subject-matter categories under section 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay factors for civil actions when transitional proceeding implicated
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party seeks a stay of a civil action alleging infringement relating to a transitional proceeding, the court shall decide whether to enter a stay based on: (A) whether a stay or denial will simplify issues and streamline trial; (B) whether discovery is complete and whether a trial date has been set; (C) whether a stay or denial would unduly prejudice the nonmoving party or present a clear tactical advantage for the moving party; and (D) whether a stay or denial will reduce the burden of litigation on the parties and the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may take immediate interlocutory appeal to the Federal Circuit; review may be de novo to ensure consistent application of precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATM exemption for venue in covered business method patent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement of a covered business method patent, an automated teller machine shall not be deemed to be a regular and established place of business for purposes of section 1400(b) of title 28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrows venue bases that might rely on ATMs as regular/established place of business for venue in patent suits involving covered business method patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: State court jurisdiction over patent/copyright claims restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: No State court shall have jurisdiction over any claim for relief arising under any Act of Congress relating to patents, plant variety protection, or copyrights. 'State' includes U.S. States, DC, Puerto Rico, USVI, American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends 28 U.S.C. §1338(a) to centralize federal jurisdiction for patent-related claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Circuit appellate jurisdiction clarified
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends 28 U.S.C. §1295(a)(1) to include appeals from final decisions of district courts (and specified territorial district courts) in any civil action arising under, or with compulsory counterclaim arising under, Acts of Congress relating to patents or plant variety protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures appeals in patent cases are taken to the Federal Circuit from a broader set of district courts/territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of patent/copyright/plant variety protection cases to federal court
rubrics_metrics.description: New 28 U.S.C. §1454: A civil action in which any party asserts a claim arising under Acts of Congress relating to patents, plant variety protection, or copyrights may be removed to the federal district court where the action is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules: if removal is based solely on this section, any party may remove and time limitations in section 1446(b) may be extended for cause shown. The removing court is not precluded from hearing claims that the state court lacked jurisdiction over. Remand rules specify remand of claims not basis for removal or outside original/supplemental jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of accused infringers — limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused infringers may be joined in one action as defendants/counterclaim defendants or have actions consolidated only if: (1) any right to relief is asserted against the parties jointly, severally, or in the alternative with respect to or arising out of the same transaction, occurrence, or series of transactions relating to making/using/importing/offering for sale/selling of the same accused product or process; and (2) questions of fact common to all defendants/counterclaim defendants will arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accused infringers may not be joined solely on allegations that they each infringed the patent(s) in suit. A party who is an accused infringer may waive these limitations with respect to that party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for procedural amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments made by this section (procedural/jurisdictional/joinder/removal provisions) shall apply to any civil action commenced on or after the date of enactment of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures clear applicability window for procedural changes; specific sections may have their own effective dates as noted in the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical amendments and removal of 'deceptive intent' language
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple sections (e.g., 116, 184, 185, 251, 253, 256) are amended to reorganize headings/paragraphs and to strike language requiring 'without deceptive intent' or similar phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are structural/terminology amendments clarifying provisions such as joint inventions, foreign filing, reissue of defective patents, correction of named inventors, and effect of reissue; they remove references to deceptive intent from statutory text where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of validity: structural revisions to section 282
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 282 is amended to reorganize the patent presumption/defenses language (inserting headings like '(a) IN GENERAL' and '(b) DEFENSES' and revising paragraph punctuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual/structural revisions were made; the Act strikes certain sentences and adjusts wording (e.g., 'uneforceability' -> 'unenforceability') to clarify statutory organization. (Full operative effect follows from the amended statutory text.)
